title: Dividing Fractions and Mixed Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Dividing Fractions Worksheets: Reciprocals and Mixed Numbers (TEKS 6.3A, 6.3E, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.2E extend representations for division to include fraction notation such as a/b represents the same number as a ÷ b where b ≠ 0; 6.3A recognize that dividing by a rational number and multiplying by its reciprocal result in equivalent values; 6.3B determine, with and without computation, whether a quantity is increased or decreased when multiplied by a fraction, including values greater than or less than one; 6.3E multiply and divide positive rational numbers fluently
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.2E, 6.3A, 6.3B and 6.3E: fraction bars, reciprocals, increase or decrease, dividing fractions and mixed numbers, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal.
key_sub: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 × 8 = 6. Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A fraction is a division: 34 = 3 ÷ 4.
  • To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 2/3 ÷ 4/5 = 2/3 × 5/4.
  • Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first.
  • Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes a positive number smaller; by a fraction greater than 1 makes it bigger.

Examples

Example

3/4 ÷ 1/8

3/4 × 8/1

24/4

Answer: 6

Example

2 1/2 ÷ 3/4

5/2 × 4/3

20/6

Answer: 3 1/3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Flipping the first fractionKeep the first fraction; flip only the divisor.
Dividing tops and bottoms without matchingMultiply by the reciprocal instead.
Thinking multiplying always makes it bigger12 × 3/4 = 9, which is less than 12.

faq.a: Recognize that dividing by a rational number and multiplying by its reciprocal result in equivalent values.
Determine, with and without computation, whether a quantity is increased or decreased when multiplied by a fraction, including values greater than or less than one.
Extend representations for division to include fraction notation such as a/b represents the same number as a ÷ b where b ≠ 0.
Dividing by 1/8 asks how many eighths fit. There are 8 in each whole, so multiply by 8.

items.q:
The bar shows 34. How many groups of 18 are in 34?
34 ÷ 18 = ?
items.e: Use eighths: 34 = 68. Each group is 1 eighth. 6 eighths make 6 ÷ 1 = 6 groups. So 34 ÷ 18 = 6. Check: 6 × 18 = 34.

items.q:
The bar shows 2. How many groups of 23 are in 2?
2 ÷ 23 = ?
items.e: Use thirds: 2 = 63. Each group is 2 thirds. 6 thirds make 6 ÷ 2 = 3 groups. So 2 ÷ 23 = 3. Check: 3 × 23 = 2.

items.q: 71 is multiplied by 98. Is the product greater than, less than or equal to 71?
items.e: 98 is greater than 1, so the product is greater than 71.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 35?
items.e: Flip it: the reciprocal is 53. Check: 35 × 53 = 1. The opposite −35 is a different idea.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 4?
items.e: Write 4 as 41. Flip it: the reciprocal is 14. Check: 4 × 14 = 1.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 17?
items.e: Flip it: the reciprocal is 7. Check: 17 × 7 = 1. (71 = 7.)

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 2 12?
items.e: Write 2 12 as 52. Flip it: the reciprocal is 25. Check: 52 × 25 = 1. Flipping only the 12 part (to get 2 + 2 = 4) is a common mistake.

items.q: 79 × ? = 1
items.e: A number times its reciprocal is 1. The reciprocal of 79 is 97: 79 × 97 = 6363 = 1. (29 is what you add to 79 to make 1, not what you multiply by.)

items.q: Which is the same as 56 ÷ 23?
c: 56 × 23
56 × 32
65 × 32
65 × 23
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 56 ÷ 23 = 56 × 32 = 1 14.

items.q: Which is the same as 38 ÷ 14?
c: 83 × 14
38 × 14
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 38 ÷ 14 = 38 × 4 = 1 12.

items.q: Which is the same as 45 ÷ 310?
c: 45 × 310
45 × 103
54 × 310
54 × 103
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 45 ÷ 310 = 45 × 103 = 2 23.

c: 12 × 56
12 × 65
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 12 ÷ 56 = 12 × 65 = 35.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 ÷ 23?
c: 14 × 23
14 × 32
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 4 ÷ 23 = 4 × 32 = 6.

items.q: Which is the same as 34 ÷ 6?
c: 34 × 16
43 × 16
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 34 ÷ 6 = 34 × 16 = 18.

items.q: Which equation shows that 23 ÷ 34 = 89 is correct?
c: 34 × 89 = 23
23 × 89 = 34
23 × 34 = 89
89 ÷ 34 = 23
items.e: Division asks: what times 34 gives 23? 34 × 89 = 23, so 23 ÷ 34 = 89 is correct.

items.q: Which equation shows that 56 ÷ 13 = 2 12 is correct?
c: 2 12 ÷ 13 = 56
56 × 13 = 2 12
56 × 2 12 = 13
13 × 2 12 = 56
items.e: Division asks: what times 13 gives 56? 13 × 2 12 = 56, so 56 ÷ 13 = 2 12 is correct.

items.q: Which equation shows that 35 ÷ 910 = 23 is correct?
c: 910 × 23 = 35
35 × 910 = 23
23 ÷ 910 = 35
35 × 23 = 910
items.e: Division asks: what times 910 gives 35? 910 × 23 = 35, so 35 ÷ 910 = 23 is correct.

items.q: Which equation shows that 12 ÷ 38 = 1 13 is correct?
c: 38 × 1 13 = 12
12 × 38 = 1 13
12 × 1 13 = 38
1 13 ÷ 38 = 12
items.e: Division asks: what times 38 gives 12? 38 × 1 13 = 12, so 12 ÷ 38 = 1 13 is correct.

items.q: Without computing, 56 ÷ 13 is ___.
items.e: You divide by a number less than 1, so the quotient is greater than 56 (it is 2 12).

items.q: Without computing, 34 ÷ 1 12 is ___.
items.e: You divide by a number greater than 1, so the quotient is less than 34 (it is 12).

items.q: Without computing, 25 ÷ 45 is ___.
items.e: You divide by a number less than 1, so the quotient is greater than 25 (it is 12).

items.q: Which quotient is greater than 1?
c: 35 ÷ 12
12 ÷ 35
13 ÷ 34
25 ÷ 12
items.e: A quotient is greater than 1 when the first number is greater than the second. 35 is greater than 12, so 35 ÷ 12 = 1 15. The others are less than 1.

items.q: Which quotient is less than 1?
c: 78 ÷ 38
34 ÷ 12
56 ÷ 23
23 ÷ 56
items.e: A quotient is less than 1 when the first number is less than the second. 23 is less than 56, so 23 ÷ 56 = 45. The others are greater than 1.

items.q: 3 friends share 12 pound of chocolate equally. How much chocolate does each friend get?
items.e: Split 12 pound into 3 equal parts: 12 ÷ 3 = 12 × 13 = 16 pound. Check: 16 × 3 = 12.

items.q: One serving of yogurt is 34 cup. How many servings are in 23 cup of yogurt?
c: 89 of a serving
12 of a serving
items.e: Find how many 34-cup servings fit in 23 cup: 23 ÷ 34 = 23 × 43 = 89 of a serving. Check: 89 × 34 = 23. There is not enough for 1 full serving, so the answer is less than 1.

items.q: A rectangular strip of land is 34 mile long. Its area is 12 square mile. How wide is it?
items.e: Area = length × width, so width = area ÷ length: 12 ÷ 34 = 12 × 43 = 23 mile. Check: 23 × 34 = 12.

items.q: A rectangular garden is 2 12 yards long. Its area is 3 34 square yards. How wide is it?
items.e: Width = area ÷ length: 3 34 ÷ 2 12 = 154 × 25 = 1 12 yards. Check: 1 12 × 2 12 = 3 34.

items.q: Aaliyah has 5 14 yards of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces that are each 34 yard long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: Find how many 34-yard pieces are in 5 14 yards: 5 14 ÷ 34 = 214 × 43 = 7 pieces. Check: 7 × 34 = 5 14.

items.q: Grace has 2 23 pounds of trail mix. She puts 13 pound in each bag. How many bags can she fill?
items.e: Find how many 13-pound bags are in 2 23 pounds: 2 23 ÷ 13 = 83 × 3 = 8 bags. Check: 8 × 13 = 2 23.

items.q: Sofia has 6 cups of flour. One batch of muffins needs 34 cup. How many batches can she make?
items.e: Find how many 34-cup amounts are in 6 cups: 6 ÷ 34 = 6 × 43 = 8 batches. Check: 8 × 34 = 6.

items.q: A pitcher holds 4 12 cups of juice. Each glass holds 34 cup. How many glasses can be filled?
items.e: Find how many 34-cup glasses are in 4 12 cups: 4 12 ÷ 34 = 92 × 43 = 6 glasses. Check: 6 × 34 = 4 12.

items.q: Luis walks 34 mile in 14 hour. At this speed, how far does he walk in 1 hour?
c: 316 mile per hour
13 mile per hour
items.e: Divide the distance by the time: 34 ÷ 14 = 34 × 4 = 3 miles per hour. Check: 3 × 14 = 34.

items.q: Ava used 38 gallon of paint to cover 34 of a wall. How much paint does the whole wall need?
items.e: 34 of the wall needs 38 gallon. Find the amount for 1 whole wall: 38 ÷ 34 = 38 × 43 = 12 gallon. Check: 12 × 34 = 38.

items.q: Isaac cuts a board 7 12 feet long into shelves that are each 1 14 feet long. How many shelves does he get?
items.e: Find how many 1 14-foot shelves are in 7 12 feet: 7 12 ÷ 1 14 = 152 × 45 = 6 shelves. Check: 6 × 1 14 = 7 12.

items.q: Isabella has 2 12 hours to study. Each practice quiz takes 56 hour. How many quizzes can she finish?
items.e: Find how many 56-hour quizzes fit in 2 12 hours: 2 12 ÷ 56 = 52 × 65 = 3 quizzes. Check: 3 × 56 = 2 12.

items.q: A cook has 5 pounds of rice. Each portion uses 23 pound. How many full portions can the cook make?
items.e: 5 ÷ 23 = 5 × 32 = 152 = 7 12 portions. Only whole portions count, so the cook can make 7 full portions (with 13 pound left over).

items.q: A track is 12 mile around. Caleb runs 2 14 miles. How many laps does he run?
items.e: Find how many 12-mile laps are in 2 14 miles: 2 14 ÷ 12 = 94 × 2 = 4 12 laps. Check: 4 12 × 12 = 2 14.

items.q: 35 of a pan of lasagna is left. 4 people share it equally. What fraction of the whole pan does each person get?
c: 320 of the pan
14 of the pan
6 23 of the pan
2 25 of the pan
items.e: Split 35 into 4 equal parts: 35 ÷ 4 = 35 × 14 = 320 of the pan. Check: 320 × 4 = 35.

items.q: A scooter uses 23 gallon of gas to go 16 miles. How many miles can it go on 1 gallon?
c: 332 mile per gallon
10 23 miles per gallon
124 mile per gallon
items.e: Divide the miles by the gallons: 16 ÷ 23 = 16 × 32 = 24 miles per gallon. Check: 24 × 23 = 16.

items.q: A poster has an area of 56 square meter. It is 23 meter wide. How long is it?
items.e: Length = area ÷ width: 56 ÷ 23 = 56 × 32 = 1 14 meters. Check: 1 14 × 23 = 56.

items.q: Ximena has 4 cups of soup. Each bowl holds 23 cup. Which expression shows how many bowls she can fill?
items.e: The question asks how many 23-cup bowls fit in 4 cups, so divide 4 by 23: 4 ÷ 23 = 4 × 32 = 6 bowls. Check: 6 × 23 = 4.

items.q: Which question can you answer with 34 ÷ 18?
c: How much is 34 cup plus 18 cup?
How many 18-cup scoops are in 34 cup?
How many 34-cup scoops are in 18 cup?
What is 18 of 34 cup?
items.e: 34 ÷ 18 asks how many eighths are in 34: 34 = 68, so 6 scoops. “18 of 34” is multiplication, and the reversed question is 18 ÷ 34.

items.q: Lucia pours 2 cups of milk into 13-cup glasses. Noah pours 2 12 cups of milk into 12-cup glasses. Who fills more glasses?
items.e: Lucia: 2 ÷ 13 = 6 glasses. Noah: 2 12 ÷ 12 = 52 × 2 = 5 glasses. 6 is more than 5, so Lucia fills more glasses. She has less milk, but 13-cup glasses are smaller.
